name: com.midmanstudio.hudman
description: Game-agnostic HUD item catalog and layout persistence. HudItemType is a code-generated enum (ScriptableObject-provider + block/priority/lock-file pattern, same shape as com.midmanstudio.utilities' EffectType) so each game contributes its own HUD item catalog without the package ever hardcoding one. HudLayoutRuntime tracks per-item position/scale/opacity/visibility and named layouts with Questly's hybrid persistence split: CaptureState/RestoreState for a host-owned snapshot, SaveToMdix/LoadFromMdix for a package-owned .mdix file. The actual dragging is not reimplemented here -- HudItemDraggableAdapter plugs a HUD item into com.midmanstudio.dragndrop's DragDropController via its uGUI adapter. Deliberately excludes anything about how a game stages its HUD-editing UI (separate scene, overlay, additive load, etc.) -- that's host-specific staging, not package concern. 0.2.0 adds HudLayoutRuntime.IsEditMode/SetEditMode/ToggleEditMode/EditModeChanged, alongside the existing Selection pattern (exiting edit mode clears the current selection too). HudItemDraggableAdapter now gates on it -- dragging is off by default and only enabled while IsEditMode is true, a real behavior change from 0.1.0 where dragging was always possible with no on/off switch at all. HudItemView gained a Runtime property and a Bound event so a sibling component whose own Awake() may run before HudItemView.Bind() (called explicitly by host bootstrap code, not from Awake()) can still reliably pick up the runtime reference once it's actually available. See com.midmanstudio.gensettings' Samples~/editHUD_hudman_integration_example.cs for the host-side wiring this was built for.
